Typical path: study nuclear engineering, electrical engineering, thermal energy, or mechanical engineering -> join a nuclear company as operations staff or inspector -> complete systematic training and gain operating experience -> earn a nuclear reactor operator license -> advance to senior operator, shift supervisor, or technical support.

Nuclear power reactor operators ensure safe reactor operation, including startup and shutdown, power adjustment, operating-parameter monitoring, routine inspections, and anomaly response. They must hold an operator license and strictly follow operating procedures, making this a core execution role in nuclear safety.

entries: Nuclear power reactor operators ensure safe reactor operation, including startup and shutdown, power adjustment, operating-parameter monitoring, routine inspections, and anomaly response. They must hold an operator license and strictly follow operating procedures.
Monitor reactor power, temperature, pressure, and other operating parameters in the main control room.
Perform reactor startup, shutdown, and power adjustments according to procedures.
Operate control rods, valves, and auxiliary systems to change operating conditions.
Regularly inspect plant equipment and record and report anomalies.
Participate in accident response and drills according to emergency plans.
Complete operating logs, shift handovers, and permit management.

paragraphs: Three-shift control-room duty is routine, with a wall of screens ahead. When a parameter changes, operators determine whether it is normal fluctuation or an abnormal signal. Operations proceed step by step through signing, confirmation, and execution, with no missing link. Before handover, operators inspect the plant in helmets and protective equipment along set routes. Before the licensing exam, they still study procedures at night.

In one sentence: monitor parameters, operate according to procedures, inspect equipment, and respond to anomalies. Duties include reactor-parameter monitoring, startup, shutdown, and power adjustment, plant inspections, emergency drills, logs, and shift handovers.
